items.author: huhoo
items.description: Table→Chart drafting: input is a table (local file, or the parsing channel’s extracted main text from scanned / cloud PDF / photo), and the output contains four sections — chart specifications (chart type / x-axis / y-axis / series; chosen by a human, not auto-selected), table-reading key points (one sentence per item; each numeric value is mapped back word-for-word to the exact header cell; attach [S#] with page number or line number), chart limitations and items not captured (missing cells and empty values / merged cells and multi-row headers / units and scope / extrapolations outside the table and unreadable items — named by category), and source with parsing date. Five automated checks: format and counts; anchors and positioning; numbers mapped back exactly to their cells (all typographic title marks in the text are restored to the table); naming the four categories of limits; investment- and rating-related assertions return zero matches. No web access; does not perform human-style recalculation. Do NOT use for: investment advice, ratings and target prices, or situations that require recomputing ratios. Triggers: table charting / chart specs / table-reading key points
items.name: cn-table-to-chart

items.author: huhoo
items.description: Investment-decision memorandum draft generator: input is a company name / six-digit code or materials you have; output are seven memo sections — Summary, Facts & Figures, Business Highlights, Risks & Bear Case, Missing Data & Open Items, Manual Review Required, Source Index. Each numeric item must include a disclosure or regulatory source plus a character/page locator; if a line cannot be retrieved, write "Not obtained". Both bull and bear points must include at least one item each or automated checks will block the output. Suitable for organizing pre-deal materials, internal discussion drafts, and situations that require every number to be verifiable against the original text. Do NOT use for: ratings, target prices, buy/sell recommendations (always "[Pending manual review]"), final resolutions (this only drafts; the user is responsible for final approval), valuation calculations (no market or position-data legs — only an applicability statement), or aggregate risk scoring. Triggers: investment-decision memo / IC memo / pre-deal materials / discussion drafts with item-level traceability.
items.name: ic-memo-cn

items.author: huhoo
items.description: Long-form foreign-language texts (German/English/French/Japanese, with authorized access) produce four types of deliverables: main draft (.md), self-contained reading version (.html), paragraph-by-paragraph reference, and a glossary of newly introduced terms; passages in doubt are placed on a question list for human review and are not forcibly machine-translated. Do NOT use for: publishing copyrighted text verbatim, or producing practice-grade legal output.
items.name: long-doc-translation

items.author: huhoo
items.description: Resume × JD bidirectional verification drafting: inputs are two documents (local files or text retrieved via a parsing channel). Output is a four-part report — one-sentence conclusion (state only which match level was reached), item-by-item alignment (for each JD requirement: one sentence stating the requirement, one sentence giving the evidence, each tagged with [S#]; both sentences must be verbatim quotes), a two-column gaps table (JD requirements with no supporting evidence in the resume; resume content that the JD does not require), and sources (file:line number or URL + parse date). Automated checks (check_fit.py) include five validations: format and item counts; double-anchoring and localization; both sides verbatim back to the original; naming the gaps; zero matches for hiring or ranking assertions; no network/web queries. Suitable for job comparison and compiling internal transfer materials. Do NOT use for: human ranking, scoring, recommending hire or rejection, or bulk resume screening. Triggers: resume vs. JD/position match verification.
items.name: cn-resume-jd-fit

items.author: huhoo
items.description: Contract clause-by-clause breakdown drafting: input is a contract body (local file or text retrieved via a parsing channel). Output is a four-part checklist — a one-sentence overview (subject, term, price — only what appears in the text), clause-by-clause key points (each item is a one-sentence excerpt from the original, tagged with [S#] plus page or line number), clauses to monitor (explicitly name seven categories: unilateral changes / automatic renewal / exclusivity / liquidated damages / dispute resolution forum / data & confidentiality / liability cap; if none are present, state "not found"), and source with analysis date. Automated checks (check_clauses.py) — five verifications: format and clause count consistency; anchors and positioning; verbatim citation matching the original; seven-category naming; and zero hits for legal opinions or enforceability assertions — no network access. Suitable for pre-signing self-check. Do NOT use for: practice-level legal advice, determinations of clause validity/effectiveness, replacing lawyer review, or ranking/scoring. Triggers: contract highlights / clause list / pre-signing self-check
items.name: cn-contract-clauses
